Egor Kaldikov's No Comply 270 Heelflip Backside Lipslide

This actually did happen today at about 13:20 CEST.

TL;DR: Wanted to avoid crashing into a kid, crashed anyway (just not into the kid), scraped new components and my knee.

[Trek](http://www.trekbikes.com/) had a demo day in a town about 9 km away from me. I wanted to test some bikes, so I decided to get on my bike and ride there. I did over 8 km out of the 9 without any problems, got a bit muddy but nothing else worth mentioning.

My route includes a short downhill part that accelerates me to about 40 km/h. Then I brake before riding over a dam because it forms a crest and it's hard to see what's on the other side, and then there's another short downhill and a flat part with good visibility. The FU happened right after I rode over the dam (at ~25 km/h). I saw a little boy on the road. He was on the left side (his right) but moved in such a way that I thought he could step into my path. I didn't want to hit him, so I started braking as hard as I could. The problem was that the road was wet (it rained shortly before my ride) and I had my weight a bit further back than I should have. Many of you now know what followed - my front wheel lost grip and got locked, sending me and the bike to the ground.

The result? I scraped one of the pedals my Secret Santa gave me (worth 56 CAD, ridden less than 100 km before that), a part of my new saddle (on my first real ride with it), and the right grip (this was fine, I'm going to replace both anyway as soon as new ones arrive). Luckily, I downshifted shortly before the crash, so there was no damage to the rear derailer.

On the bright side, I did get to that place, rode 5 bikes (worth >$3k-5k each), and won a water bottle and a T-shirt :-)
